meta.title: AI / LLM Threat Landscape 2026
meta.scope: Cyber threat intelligence focused on AI, LLM, GenAI and agentic systems
meta.methodology: Evidence-first synthesis using primary vendor, standards-body and research sources. Metrics retain their original population/time window and are not generalized beyond it.

domains.name: AI as active operator
domains.summary: Public reporting now includes campaigns and malware where AI participates in live execution, task chaining or runtime decision-making rather than only preparation.

domains.name: AI as offensive force multiplier
domains.summary: Threat actors use AI for reconnaissance, social engineering, code generation, debugging, translation and rapid iteration.

domains.name: Prompt injection and content-borne attacks
domains.summary: Prompt Injection remains OWASP LLM01:2026, while Check Point observed a sharp rise in longer malicious payloads consistent with indirect/content-borne attack paths.

domains.name: Agentic autonomy, identity and tool abuse
domains.summary: Excessive Agency moved to LLM03:2026 and OWASP maintains a separate Agentic Top 10 covering goal hijack, tool misuse, identity abuse, memory poisoning, inter-agent communication and rogue agents.

domains.name: AI and software supply chain
domains.summary: Open-source packages, CI/CD, AI frameworks, model artifacts and gateways increasingly sit in the blast radius of supply-chain compromise.

domains.name: Enterprise AI data exposure and Shadow AI
domains.summary: Everyday enterprise AI use creates measurable data-exposure risk even without an external attacker.

domains.name: Cloud and identity abuse around AI workloads
domains.summary: Cloud-conscious eCrime increased while vendor reporting continues to emphasize stolen or misused credentials over direct infrastructure exploitation.

domains.name: Ransomware and data-extortion industrialization
domains.summary: Ransomware reporting shows greater victim volume and a shift toward high-volume data theft and extortion, with AI contributing to speed and scale in the broader ecosystem.

domains.name: Model integrity and safety-control fragility
domains.summary: Research on open-weight models demonstrates that some refusal behaviors can depend on surprisingly concentrated internal mechanisms, reinforcing that model alignment alone is not a system security boundary.

domains.name: AI coding-assistant workspace and config abuse
domains.summary: Malware now hides in assistant and IDE directories (.claude/, .vscode/, .cursor/), abuses agent hooks and configs, and prompt-injects LLM scanners. Agent configuration is attack surface.

domains.name: MCP transport and framework command injection
domains.summary: Prompt-injectable tool parameters and unsanitized STDIO config reached code execution in Semantic Kernel, LiteLLM and other MCP-consuming products in 2026. Some vendors treat the STDIO behaviour as by design.
signals: STDIO server config from untrusted input
defensive_focus: validate tool parameters outside the model
never build STDIO commands from untrusted input

domains.name: AI-assisted tooling against Latin American targets
domains.summary: Three 2026 primary reports describe operators speeding tool development or command execution with LLMs against Brazilian financial and Latin American government targets. AI use is mostly inferred from artifacts; initial access and fraud mechanics are unchanged.
signals: agentic CLI tools supervised by an operator

notable_cases.name: CLOSEDQUORUM
notable_cases.summary: Cisco Talos reported an autonomous AI C2 implant discovered through CAIRN. Talos explicitly states it did not have confirmation of in-the-wild deployment.

notable_cases.name: VoidLink
notable_cases.summary: Check Point Research reported a roughly 88,000-line functional malware framework produced by one developer with an AI coding environment in under a week.

notable_cases.name: Promptware Kill Chain
notable_cases.summary: A 2026 academic paper proposed promptware as a framework for multi-stage attacks against LLM-based systems; CSA subsequently published defensive analysis around the concept.

notable_cases.name: STARDUST CHOLLIMA / Mastra AI supply chain
notable_cases.summary: CrowdStrike reported a malicious npm dependency injected into at least 131 Mastra AI framework packages.

notable_cases.name: Perturbation Probing of LLM Safety
notable_cases.summary: Unit 42 reported that in Qwen3-4B, 50 of 350,208 feed-forward neurons were causally linked to the tested refusal template, illustrating concentrated safety behavior in that model and experiment.

notable_cases.name: DUSTMAKER
notable_cases.summary: Credential stealer that hides in AI assistant workspaces and prompt-injects LLM scanners.

notable_cases.name: Semantic Kernel prompt-to-RCE (CVE-2026-26030, CVE-2026-25592)
notable_cases.summary: Model-controlled parameters reached eval() and file helpers; fixed in 1.39.4 and 1.71.0.

research_queue.claim: A financially motivated operator breached 27 companies at an average AI-compute cost of USD 25.46 per target.
research_queue.reason: Found in secondary reporting; retain as a lead until a primary technical report is attached.

research_queue.claim: 40% of 10,000 MCP servers reviewed had security weaknesses.
research_queue.reason: Do not publish as a headline metric until the underlying Lakera methodology/source is attached and scoped.

research_queue.claim: CISA/Five Eyes designated prompt injection as the principal unresolved threat for agentic AI.
research_queue.reason: Strong wording requires the exact joint guidance before promotion.

research_queue.claim: Anthropic's September 2026 threat report names GTG-2002, GTG-10007, GTG-20006, GTG-50014 and GTG-50020 with victim counts (e.g. ~50 orgs, ~30 AI vendors, 1.8M Android app users).
research_queue.reason: Details come from press coverage; attach the primary Anthropic report before promoting actors or numbers. Reported group IDs also differ between secondary summaries.

research_queue.claim: OX Security's MCP STDIO advisory lists further CVEs (Agent Zero, Upsonic, Flowise, DocsGPT, GPT Researcher, LangBot).
research_queue.reason: Identifiers were not cross-checked against NVD/GHSA; only CVE-2026-30623 and CVE-2026-30615 are recorded.

research_queue.claim: AI website builders were used to clone Brazilian government sites for Pix payment scams (Zscaler ThreatLabz, August 2025).
research_queue.reason: Known only through press coverage here; attach the primary Zscaler report before promoting.

research_queue.claim: 80% of Brazilians have encountered deepfakes online (Veriff, Kantar survey of 1,000 respondents, February 2026).
research_queue.reason: Opinion survey from a vendor, not threat telemetry; do not use as a threat metric.

research_queue.claim: 28 million Pix scam cases in the first nine months of 2025 and a 126% rise in deepfake fraud (Rio Times citing Serasa Experian).
research_queue.reason: Not verified against Serasa or Banco Central primary data.

research_queue.claim: PixRevolution Android banking trojan targets Pix with an operator-in-the-loop model that a human or AI agent could drive (Recorded Future H1 2026).
research_queue.reason: The report raises an AI operator as a possibility; it is not an established finding.
